question.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}=\{v,w\}$ and ${A}_{2}=\{w,x,y\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{v,w\}\cap \{w,x,y\}=\{w\}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}=\{(v,1),(w,1)\} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}=\{(w,2),(x,2),(y,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & =\{v,w\}⊔\{w,x,y\} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & =\{(v,1),(w,1)\}\cup \{(w,2),(x,2),(y,2)\} \\  & =\{(v,1),(w,1),(w,2),(x,2),(y,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$
